GOALS.label: Muscle Growth
GOALS.blurb: Build size with high-quality volume and double progression

GOALS.label: Strength
GOALS.blurb: Move more weight on the big lifts — lower reps, longer rests

GOALS.label: Fat Loss
GOALS.blurb: Hold onto muscle while dieting — training defends what you built

GOALS.label: Support Another Sport
GOALS.blurb: Lifting that makes you better at your sport — without stealing its recovery

GOALS.label: General Fitness
GOALS.blurb: Balanced full-body training you can sustain for years

EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.label: Beginner
EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.blurb: New to lifting, or back after a long time off — learning the movements

EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.label: Intermediate
EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.blurb: A year or two of consistent training — the big lifts feel familiar

EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.label: Advanced
EXPERIENCE_LEVELS.blurb: Years under the bar — you know your body and progress is hard-won

EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.label: Full gym
EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.blurb: Barbells, machines, cables, dumbbells — the works

EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.label: Home gym
EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.blurb: A rack, barbell and some plates; maybe a few dumbbells

EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.label: Dumbbells only
EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.blurb: A pair (or a set) of dumbbells and a bench

EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.label: Minimal / bands
EQUIPMENT_ACCESS.blurb: Bodyweight, bands, the odd dumbbell — travel or home light

RACE_PROXIMITY.label: No date yet
RACE_PROXIMITY.blurb: Base training — the best window for heavier strength work

RACE_PROXIMITY.label: Within 8 weeks
RACE_PROXIMITY.blurb: Race-specific: strength holds, volume comes down, the block ends easy

RACE_PROXIMITY.label: 3–4 months
RACE_PROXIMITY.blurb: Build first, then hold while your sport takes priority

RACE_PROXIMITY.label: 5–6 months
RACE_PROXIMITY.blurb: Plenty of runway — this block is all build

ENDURANCE_LOADS.label: Under 4 hours
ENDURANCE_LOADS.blurb: Low interference — room for 2–3 lifting days and heavier loading

ENDURANCE_LOADS.label: 4–7 hours
ENDURANCE_LOADS.blurb: Moderate — two lifting days at a controlled dose is the sweet spot

ENDURANCE_LOADS.label: 8–11 hours
ENDURANCE_LOADS.blurb: High — lifting caps at two short sessions and stops growing

ENDURANCE_LOADS.label: 12+ hours
ENDURANCE_LOADS.blurb: Very high — minimum effective dose purely to hold what you have

DISCIPLINES.label: Swim
DISCIPLINES.blurb: Biases toward lat/upper-back pulling strength and posterior-shoulder balance

DISCIPLINES.label: Bike
DISCIPLINES.blurb: Biases toward hip-extension force — heavier squat/hinge and single-leg work

DISCIPLINES.label: Run
DISCIPLINES.blurb: Biases toward tendon stiffness, pelvic stability and eccentric control

DISCIPLINES.label: Fairly even
DISCIPLINES.blurb: Balanced template — no discipline gets extra slots

INJURY_AREAS.label: Knee
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No squats, lunges or leg extensions; pressing and hinging carry the legs

INJURY_AREAS.label: Shoulder
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No overhead pressing or dips; horizontal pressing and raises stay

INJURY_AREAS.label: Lower back
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No barbell hinges or squats; supported machine work covers the posterior chain

INJURY_AREAS.label: Hip
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No deep lunging or heavy hinging; machines and hip thrusts carry it

INJURY_AREAS.label: Elbow
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No skull-crushers or dips; cable pressdowns and neutral-grip pulls stay

INJURY_AREAS.label: Wrist
INJURY_AREAS.blurb: No barbell pressing or wrist curls; neutral-grip and machine work instead

intro.label: Intro
intro.blurb: Learn the movements at easy loads — this week is practice, not a test

recovery.label: Recovery
recovery.blurb: Easy re-entry week — lighter loads, groove the movements

accumulation.label: Build
accumulation.blurb: Add reps and sets — accumulate productive volume

intensification.label: Push
intensification.blurb: Loads climb, effort climbs — chase the top of every rep range

peak.label: Peak
peak.blurb: Heaviest work of the block — low reps, full recovery between sets

deload.label: Deload
deload.blurb: Planned easy week — ~10% lighter so you rebound stronger

maintenance.label: Maintain
maintenance.blurb: Loads held, volume trimmed — your sport takes priority this week

race-week.label: Race week
race-week.blurb: One short session early in the week, then nothing. Show up fresh

output.err: A block needs at least one week.
Blocks longer than 12 weeks outrun any plan — split this into two blocks.
A block needs at least one week of real training.
Intro and recovery weeks only make sense at the start of a block, before the training proper.
More than 2 easy opening weeks stops being an introduction and starts being the block.
One race week per block — a second race needs its own block.
Race week is the last week of the block — nothing gets programmed past the start line.
More than 2 easy weeks in a row stops being a taper and starts being detraining.
Deload weeks close the block — training on tired legs after an easy week wastes both.
A deload needs at least 3 productive weeks before it — there's no fatigue to shed yet.
